items.review_rationale: Read piecewise real absolute value under the total order of reals, its nonnegative property and derived metric difference; distinguished rational absolute value from real-valued context.

references.phrase: piecewise sign condition x≥0 versus x<0
references.context: Order comparison selecting x or its additive inverse −x.
Piecewise map from real x to x if nonnegative and −x otherwise.
Nonnegative real magnitude of the difference between a and b.

references.disposition: The piecewise definition entails |x|≥0; distance interpretation is an accompanying consequence.

items.review_rationale: Read derivative at an interior real point by finite limit of the nonzero-increment difference quotient, including restriction a+h in I, not differentiability of arbitrary endpoint functions.

references.context: Ratio of function increment over nonzero real increment h, with both evaluation arguments in domain.
Punctured approach of real increments toward zero while a+h remains in the domain.

references.disposition: Derivative is defined only if the difference quotient approaches a finite real number.

items.review_rationale: Read finite real limit with function defined on punctured neighborhood, epsilon-delta quantifier order, strict positivity and puncture excluding a, retaining interval domain restriction.

references.context: Points x in a chosen open interval with x≠a and 0<|x−a|<δ.
For every ε>0 there is δ>0 such that each permitted x has |f(x)−L|<ε.

references.disposition: Only punctured domain values are used, so the value at a need not exist or equal L.

items.review_rationale: Read complex inner product over a complex vector space using positive-definite Hermitian form, linearity in first slot, conjugate linearity in second and explicit convention.

references.context: Scalars are complex numbers with complex conjugation, needed for Hermitian sesquilinearity.
Form linear in the first argument, conjugate-linear in the second and conjugate symmetric across slots.
For every nonzero v, ⟨v,v⟩ is strictly positive real, and ⟨v,v⟩=0 iff v=0.

references.disposition: This is one of two standard conventions; this source explicitly chooses first-slot linearity, not second-slot linearity.
